content.comment_body: Hello, I have a quick question: Is it possible to connect Modbus RTU to a [product_name] [version_no]? If not, are there alternative options such as using Modbus IP or others? If yes, how can this be implemented? Thank you. (Split from discussion about [product_name] modbus RTU communication.)
The [product_name] [article_no] does not support Modbus, EIB/KNX bus, AS-i bus, or similar. It only supports TCP/IP with the [version_no] protocol.
Is there any workaround for this issue? Perhaps through some type of converter? Thank you in advance.

What you need is a device that communicates using Modbus RTU on one side and [version_no] protocol via TCP/IP on the other. Some HMIs may offer this functionality, but they might exceed your budget. Try searching online for suitable hardware. Hope this helps.

I discovered an Arduino project capable of reading both Modbus IP and RTU protocols. My question is how to convert Modbus RTU to the protocol that [product_name] [version_no] understands. Is it possible to reverse engineer the communication protocol to make this work? Ideally, I want to replicate the functionality of high-priced HMIs with a much more affordable chip. If successful, this could be a cost-effective solution. Thank you in advance.
Regarding your mention of the [version_no] protocol, are you referring to Profinet or a different lower-level ethernet-based protocol used by [product_name] [version_no]? Thanks.
A budget-friendly method for Modbus RTU communication would be to switch to a [version_no] device, which can then communicate with your [product_name].
Thank you. I have decided to fully implement a [version_no] system from scratch. I appreciate everyone's help and support.

analysis.insight_summary: The central problem is the lack of Modbus RTU support in the [product_name] [version_no], which complicates integration with Modbus RTU devices. Users are seeking alternative solutions such as protocol converters or switching to other hardware. The discussion underlines the need for improved protocol compatibility and clearer information regarding available interfaces.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] [version_no] to support Modbus RTU natively or provide straightforward alternatives for Modbus communication. They look for transparent information on compatible protocols and accessible, cost-effective solutions for protocol conversion.
